correctness.rationale: The domain D is a vertical two-fold tile of Q=(0,1)x(0,1/4). Its displaced second point relative to Q is a/4 with a in {1,2,3}, all occurring on positive-area subsets; thus unfolding is unitary L²(D)→L²(Q;C²). Fourier factors (n,4m) have squared norm |Q|=1/4, and each two-coset fiber is [[1,1],[1,exp(2πita/4)]] up to a unitary phase. Its squared singular values are 2±2|cos(πat/4)|, giving exact normalized global bounds (1±rho)/2 with rho=max_{a=1,2,3}|cos(πat/4)|. Localized Fourier approximation proves sharpness, invertible fibers prove onto, and a singular positive-measure displacement destroys the Riesz basis: t≡0,4/3,2,8/3 modulo 4. Elementary trigonometric interval inequalities prove unique minimax t≡1,3, rho=1/√2 and squared ratio 3+2√2. Taylor expansion at the four collisions gives sharp quadratic coefficients π²a0²/64. Independently checked all three geometric displacements, exact singular Gram eigenvalues, 10,001-offset grid and quadratic constants; continuum proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Bounded checks corroborate; unrestricted claim depends on analytical proof.
